tagline: The red city — where Jemaa el-Fnaa's storytellers and snake charmers fill the square and the medina's souks run for miles.
overview: Marrakesh has performed the same evening miracle for 900 years: as the sun drops, Jemaa el-Fnaa square fills with drummers, storytellers, snake charmers and a hundred grill stalls — the world's oldest nightly street theatre.

Behind it, the medina's souks run for miles through copper, leather and carpet quarter lanes; the 12th-century Koutoubia minaret guides you home; and the Bahia Palace and Ben Youssef Madrasa hold Morocco's most dazzling tilework. Yves Saint Laurent's Majorelle Garden keeps its famous cobalt blue.
Speed's 2025 Africa tour streamed from Marrakesh. The Atlas Mountains rise an hour south — and riads (courtyard guesthouses) hidden behind blank medina walls are the place to stay.

funFacts.title: THE RED CITY
funFacts.text: Medina walls and buildings were ordered clay-pink in the 12th century — the colour is law.

funFacts.title: THE KOUTOUBIA
funFacts.text: The 77m minaret has guided travellers for 800 years — no building may exceed it.
